items.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06
items.q: the nearest thing to me was, say, Pete Fountain, Ken Collier. And Pete was older than I was, you know. Charlie I didn't know at the time.

ctx.x: Yeah, why don't you take it?

Okay. Well, anyway, I had started playing tenor guitar, and this whole thing happened with the banjo, and started meeting, you know, it's an interesting thing. I was thinking while I was walking over there, that I had no peer group as a kid. It's very important that you have a peer group, people you grow up with like interests, and you kind of bounce things off of each other, bounce off of each other sometimes. That's important. I didn't really have that, because I was so lonely in this, you know? I mean, the…
Very witty singer too, wasn't he? Great, great, yeah.
